Preparations for plant-level readiness formed an additional important part of Task 2. The project identified the signals, communication pathways, and plant-level configuration required to activate grid-forming modes in a safe and controlled manner. This included mapping interactions between inverter-level inverter controls and plant-level supervisory functions, defining start-up dependencies, establishing the transitions between grid-following and grid-forming modes, and outlining conditions for enabling GFM operation under weak-grid conditions. Preliminary commissioning workflows were developed to guide the eventual activation of GFM functions. These workflows detail the prerequisites for enabling GFM operation, including protection settings, plant-level reference alignments, and inverter-mode transition logic, and describe verification steps that must be completed during commissioning to ensure stable operation. These preparations reduce the risk of unexpected behavior during initial synchronization and support the safe introduction of GFM functionality into a multi-resource hybrid plant. Through these activities, Task 2 translated analytical findings into actionable engineering procedures and established a coherent path toward a controlled, safe, and technically rigorous field demonstration. The work completed under Task 2 provides the operational framework necessary to move from validated simulation to real-world activation of grid-forming capabilities. 7.3 Task 3 - Model and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Testbed Development Task 3 established the modeling, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) infrastructure required to evaluate mixed grid-forming and grid-following inverter controls within the Wheatridge hybrid plant. This work served as the technical backbone for all EMT validation, control-interaction studies, and future commissioning activities. The effort combined high-fidelity EMT model development, plant-level supervisory integration, and real-time controller testing into a single, coherent modeling framework suitable for both engineering design and system-level performance evaluation. Page 13 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric At the inverter level, detailed EMT models were constructed for the grid-forming BESS and grid-forming Type-3 wind turbine generators, including converter switching behavior, inner-loop current control, DC-link dynamics, current-limiting functions, and voltage-forming mechanisms. These models were tuned to capture the characteristic responses essential to evaluating GFM behavior, such as active- power/angle regulation, voltage stiffness, and the interaction between current limits and disturbance recovery. Complementary EMT models were created for the GFL wind turbines and solar PV resources to allow full-plant interaction studies under common electrical conditions. All resource models were validated through steady- state checks, initialization testing, and disturbance-case comparisons to ensure numerical stability and physical realism. The EMT models were then integrated into a generic hybrid-plant simulation environment incorporating the electrical network, plant-level supervisory controls, dispatch functions, and reference-coordination logic. Particular attention was given to frequency- and voltage-control hierarchies, hand-off between GFM and GFL modes, and the synchronization requirements associated with GFM operation in a weak-grid environment.
